requiredEdit.finding: The installed Playwright 1.57.0 list/line reporter emits a summary word the U9b PLAYWRIGHT_SUMMARY regex did not recognise: `interrupted`. Because an unmatched line is skipped by `if (!summary) continue;`, a run printing `  1 interrupted` alongside `  2 passed (...)` with no explicit `failed` line archived 2/0 and read SATISFIED - a FALSE SATISFIED, the one direction this contract must never fail in, and the exact inverse of the module's own stated fail-closed posture.
whatChanged: PLAYWRIGHT_SUMMARY's alternation gained `interrupted`, which routes into the existing `else if (summary[2] !== 'skipped') failed += ...` branch, so an interrupted row counts as FAILED exactly as `flaky` and `did not run` already do.

A second missed token was found by reading generateSummaryMessage directly in this pass (see reporterSummaryVocabulary below) and covered the same way: the fatal-error token, which counts ERRORS rather than tests. A new PLAYWRIGHT_FATAL_ERRORS regex matches both of its spellings and adds its count to `failed`. It is tested FIRST in the loop, before PLAYWRIGHT_SUMMARY, because no branch below could read it and letting it fall through would discard it silently in exactly the way `interrupted` was.
The two doc comments over the regexes and over parseRunnerOutput were rewritten to say six words rather than five and to name the fatal-error token and why each counts as failed.

Four new pin cases: two rerun-branch cases driving the injected runner end to end (interruption, fatal error) and two it.each rows over parseRunnerOutput (interrupted, the plural fatal-error spelling).

All 35 pin cases from PR #1815 head pass unchanged.

behaviour: The narrow successor of U9 (FN-u9-rerun-parser-expects-labeled-line). --rerun reads the ladder runner's real output for the single group it just ran: parseRunnerOutput({ group, output }) accepts the existing labelled `<group>: N passed` form first, and falling back to that, parses Playwright's bare summary lines and attributes them to that group. `passed` adds to passed; `failed`, `flaky`, `did not run`, `interrupted` and a fatal error outside any test all add to failed; `skipped` counts as neither; output with no summary line at all stays 0/0 and can never be coverage. Nothing else in the contract moved.

designDecisions.decision: The labelled form keeps precedence over the bare summary.
designDecisions.why: The charter requires the labelled form to stay accepted. Reading it first means an injected runner, or any future runner that prefixes its group, is read exactly as U9 read it, and the bare-summary branch is reached only when no labelled row names this group.

A row that went green only on retry is not 'the staged subset ran clean against this exact commit', which is the only thing E2E-80 accepts. Pinned by 'archives 2/1 and stays MISSING when the summary reports a flake'.

designDecisions.decision: `did not run` counts as FAILED; `skipped` counts as neither.
designDecisions.why: An aborted run left tests unexecuted, so the group is not proven - fail-closed. A declared skip is not a failure and must not be able to zero out a real pass. Both pinned in the runner-output-reader table.

designDecisions.decision: The summary is attributed to the ONE group --rerun just ran, with no further evidence that the numbers belong to it.
designDecisions.why: runGroup spawns the runner once per group with `--group=<name>`, so nothing else can be in that child's output. Sound only under that one-group-per-invocation property; named in findingsReportedNotFixed F7 rather than defended by code. Lane A independently confirmed F7's shape and agreed it is not currently reachable.

designDecisions.decision: The summary regex requires the line to be nothing but the count, the word, and - for `passed` only - a parenthesised duration.
designDecisions.why: So the parser cannot become greedy while learning the bare form. 'Running 3 tests using 1 worker' is not a summary and is pinned as 0/0; the seven ANSI-coloured web-server lines in the verbatim fixture start with an escape byte and never match.

designDecisions.decision: The captured fixture is built by code point (String.fromCharCode) and interpolated, not written as \u escapes.
designDecisions.why: `npx oxfmt` REWRITES a \u escape back into the literal character, which turned the pin source into a file carrying raw ESC bytes - invisible in a diff and hostile to review. Naming ESC / MICRO / ANGLE keeps the source pure ASCII and the emitted bytes identical.

designDecisions.decision: `interrupted` counts as FAILED, on the same footing as `flaky` and `did not run`.
designDecisions.why: Lane A's required edit. An interrupted test never produced a result, so the group is not proven clean on this commit; counting it as failed is the only reading that keeps the module's stated posture ('everything here fails closed'). Adding the word to the alternation is sufficient - the existing non-passed, non-skipped branch does the counting - so this is a one-token behaviour change, not a new code path. Pinned twice: once through the archive and CLI line, once directly on parseRunnerOutput.

designDecisions.decision: The fatal-error token is matched by its own regex, checked BEFORE the summary regex, and its count is added to `failed`.
designDecisions.why: It is the one summary token that is not an outcome word and not a count of tests, so it cannot be folded into PLAYWRIGHT_SUMMARY's alternation without making that pattern's shape a lie. It is checked first because a `continue` after a failed match is exactly the silent-drop mechanism that produced the `interrupted` defect - ordering the explicit match ahead of the fall-through guard makes the drop impossible. Counting errors as failures is fail-closed and cannot invent coverage: the worst it can do is refuse a run that a human would have accepted.
designDecisions.alternativeRejected: Ignoring the token, on the ground that a fatal error outside any test is not a test failure. Rejected: Playwright pushes it only when at least one test ran, i.e. it appears exactly beside a `N passed` line, which is precisely the false-SATISFIED shape Lane A found.

nonClaims: The REAL LADDER RUNNER WAS NOT SPAWNED in this lane, and no Playwright process ran. The charter forbids it here. Every rerun case injects a fake runner that reprints captured or transcribed bytes; the fix is proven against the recorded spelling of one real run plus the reporter's own source, not against a live Playwright. The parent's main proof is the first real exercise of this branch.

NO REAL RUN PRINTING `interrupted` OR A FATAL-ERROR LINE HAS BEEN OBSERVED IN THIS REPO. Both new behaviours are proven against generateSummaryMessage's source as read in this pass (playwright 1.57.0), and the pin fixtures are its format strings with their interpolations filled in - not captured bytes. If a future Playwright changed either spelling, this pin would still pass and the real rerun would silently stop reading the line. Both directions are fail-closed, so the failure mode is a false MISSING, never a false SATISFIED.

Counting a fatal error as `failed` is a JUDGEMENT, recorded as D8, not a measurement. Playwright itself does not call it a test failure; this contract treats it as one because the run did not complete clean. The number it adds is a count of errors, not of tests, so an archived `failed` count from that branch is not a test count.

Because the REAL_RUNNER_TAIL fixture is one captured run's bytes, a future Playwright version that changes its summary wording would pass this pin and still break the real rerun. The pin holds the spelling that exists today.
Enforcement is still PROCEDURAL, by the loop (PK-e2e-80-ci-wiring). Nothing runs this contract automatically - there is no workflow job and no hook.

The contract still reads RECEIPTS, not runs. It cannot detect a receipt reporting a run that did not happen; it can only refuse to count one it cannot read, one for the wrong commit, one that failed, or one that passed nothing.

No coverage was created. The contract reads MISSING at this baseline and at every merge commit in the ledger, because no main-proof receipt has ever recorded a passing smoke, fixture-smoke or membership-smoke group (U9 finding F3, unchanged).
The default archive dir is still gitignored (U9 finding F2), so an archive receipt written by --rerun still does not reach main on its own.

findingsReportedNotFixed.F6: `npx oxfmt` REWRITES a \u escape sequence in a string literal into the literal character it names, so a fixture that deliberately carries control bytes cannot be written as \u escapes. The workaround this unit uses is String.fromCharCode plus template interpolation. Unchanged in revision 2 - the new fixtures are pure ASCII and need no workaround.
findingsReportedNotFixed.F7: The runner's one-group-per-invocation property is what makes attributing a bare summary to a group sound, and nothing enforces it. Lane A independently traced buildRunPlan and confirmed the property holds today (one --group, one Playwright invocation, one summary block) and that the risk is real in shape but not currently reachable. Enforcing it would mean changing the core module, which this unit does not own.
findingsReportedNotFixed.F8: U9's F1-F5 all still stand and none are addressed here: SPEC_BY_GROUP is still not exported (F1); the default archive dir is still gitignored (F2); no receipt in the ledger has ever proved smoke, fixture-smoke or membership-smoke on an exact commit (F3); `runtime.playwright` is still not a consistently machine-readable field across the ledger's receipts (F4); the top-level-CLI-pollutes-stdout hazard for scripts/qc modules is unchanged (F5).
findingsReportedNotFixed.F9: The oxlint units config reports '64 rules' for both files in this lane, where U9's receipt recorded '65 rules' for the pin. Both runs report 0 warnings and 0 errors, so nothing is hidden, but the two receipts disagree about the rule count and this lane did not investigate which is right.
findingsReportedNotFixed.F10: NEW in revision 2. The parser now knows every line generateSummaryMessage can emit at Playwright 1.57.0, and that completeness is a snapshot, not a contract: nothing in this repo pins the reporter's vocabulary to the version installed, so a Playwright upgrade could add a seventh word and reintroduce exactly the defect Lane A found. A durable fix would read the vocabulary from the installed reporter, or assert the parser against a generated summary rather than a transcribed one. Out of scope for this narrow successor unit and reported rather than attempted.
